name: Flint
purpose: Mixture-of-experts language model for coding agents: investigates codebases, fixes bugs, implements features and writes tests; supports reasoning and multi-turn tool use (card).

license.name: Apache-2.0
license.notes: Apache License 2.0 text read in the repo LICENSE file: commercial use, modification and redistribution allowed with notice and patent grant.

architecture.kind: decoder-only MoE, 2 dense then 47 MoE layers, sliding-window plus full attention
architecture.attention: 35 sliding-window layers (513 tokens) and 14 full-attention layers; 32 Q / 4 KV heads, head dim 128, per-head QK RMSNorm and learned attention sinks; RoPE on sliding layers only

variants.notes: UD-IQ2_XXS 11.86, UD-Q2_K_XL 13.56, UD-Q6_K_XL 36.32, Q8_0 42.3 GB; 352k downloads

pc-12gb.notes: 25.05 GB file against 9.6 GB VRAM plus 50 GB RAM budget; experts stream from RAM (~2.5 B active, decode bound by RAM bandwidth)

pc-16gb.notes: 25.05 GB file against 13.6 GB VRAM plus 50 GB RAM budget; experts stream from RAM (~2.5 B active, decode bound by RAM bandwidth)

pc-24gb.notes: 25.05 GB file against 21.6 GB VRAM plus 82 GB RAM budget; experts stream from RAM (~2.5 B active, decode bound by RAM bandwidth)

pc-32gb.notes: 25.05 GB file fits the VRAM budget (29.6 GB) with room for KV

mac-16-24gb.notes: 25.05 GB file against a GPU share of about 12 GB (KV cache not included)

mac-32gb.notes: 25.05 GB file against a GPU share of about 22 GB (KV cache not included)

mac-64gb+.notes: 25.05 GB file against a GPU share of about 52 GB (KV cache not included)

other: LM Studio and ggml-org GGUF repos exist
engine_support.notes: ggml-org, unsloth, lmstudio-community and bartowski publish GGUFs, so llama.cpp support exists; exact version not checked.

benchmarks.name: Terminal-Bench 2.1 (Terminus 2)
benchmarks.variant: BF16, pass@1 over >=5 attempts, temp 1.0; web-retrieved solutions counted as failures

benchmarks.name: SWE-bench Pro v2 (mini-swe-agent)
benchmarks.variant: BF16, as stated in the card text; a score this high for a 2.5B-active model is unusual and is not cross-checked

strengths: 2.5B active parameters: cheap decode, 25 GB at the Q4 level so it sits in 16 GB VRAM plus RAM
sliding-window attention on 35 of 49 layers keeps the KV cache small at long context
trained for terminal and repository agent work
weaknesses: only vendor numbers; comparison scores of other models in the card image are developer-reported
vendor serves it on a single B300 or H200, local quality at Q4 not measured
soft.behavior: reasoning and tool use; sampling temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95, top-k 20 used for the vendor results
soft.maturity: new vendor (Recursive); strong uptake: 62k downloads and 1.4k likes of the main repo, 352k of the unsloth GGUF

tona_fit.reason: A 40B-A2.5B agentic coder with Apache-2.0 (text read), small active set and cheap long-context attention is close to the shape our reference box serves best. Quality is unproven outside the vendor table (Terminal-Bench 2.1 54.9 is in the Qwen3.6-35B-A3B class), so it needs our own coding eval against Qwen3.8-27B and Ornith.
blockers: implementation needed (sliding window with attention sinks, 256 experts)

open_questions: meaning of 'SWE-bench Pro v2 89.7' versus other Pro scores
Q4 quality loss on agentic tasks
builder's reasons for the sink and no-position full-attention layers
